pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The sender’s request
paragraphs: The sender writes, “Please send a quick reply so I can plan the next stage.” They need to know that the request has arrived and when they can expect a complete answer.

The phrase “quick reply” does not specify whether an acknowledgement is enough. The sender has not explicitly asked for unchecked figures, but the recipient is unsure what level of detail is expected immediately.

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The receiver’s concern
paragraphs: The receiver needs more time to verify the figures before sending a complete answer. They cannot provide checked figures immediately, but they can acknowledge receipt and give a realistic reply time.
Acknowledging a request and completing the checks are separate actions. The receiver can therefore keep the sender informed without presenting unverified figures as final.

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: Quick acknowledgement, not unchecked certainty. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I think my request for a quick reply has been misunderstood. I wasn’t asking for the checked figures today. I was asking for a prompt acknowledgement and a realistic time for the complete answer. If verification takes until four tomorrow, please say that. What’s difficult is silence, followed by a rushed answer that looks final but hasn’t been checked. Could you explain both positions again so they can see the common ground? One person is protecting accuracy; the other is trying to plan around a response. A useful reformulation should make those needs visible and give an example, rather than repeat the word quick more loudly. Please check that they agree with your summary before treating it as their settled position

s_mission.title: A request and a misunderstanding

questions.prompt: Why does the sender need a quick reply?
questions.answer: The sender needs it to plan the next stage.
questions.hint: Find the reason in the opening sentence.

questions.prompt: What does the receiver mistakenly think “quick reply” requires?
questions.answer: They think it requires sending final figures immediately.
questions.hint: Identify the receiver’s interpretation in paragraph two.

questions.prompt: Which two things can the sender receive before the figures are checked?
questions.answer: The sender can receive acknowledgement and a realistic time for a complete answer.
questions.hint: Return to the sender’s two needs in paragraph one.

referenceParagraphs: The sender asks for a quick reply because they need to plan the next stage. They need acknowledgement that the request arrived and a realistic time for a complete answer.

The receiver thinks “quick reply” means sending final figures immediately. Those figures still need verification, so the receiver cannot yet provide a complete, checked answer. An acknowledgement does not require those checks to be finished.

s_reply.title: An acknowledgement and a realistic deadline

questions.prompt: What does Kim suggest sending now?
questions.answer: She suggests sending an acknowledgement and a realistic time for the complete answer.
questions.hint: Find the two parts of Kim’s suggestion in paragraph one.

questions.prompt: When is it acceptable to promise an answer by 4 pm tomorrow?
questions.answer: It is acceptable only if that deadline is achievable.
questions.hint: Look for the condition attached to the time.

questions.prompt: What should happen if the checks take longer than expected?
questions.answer: The person checking should send an update with a revised time.
questions.hint: Find the action that replaces silence.

s_reply.referenceLabel: An acknowledgement and a realistic deadline
referenceParagraphs: Kim suggests acknowledging the request now and giving a realistic time for the complete answer. The person checking the figures can say “by 4 pm tomorrow” only if that deadline is achievable.

If the checks take longer than expected, they should send an update with a revised time rather than remain silent. Acknowledgement confirms receipt; it does not mean that the figures have already been verified.
